name: Word Rotator
description: "Built for ___" rolls its gradient word through four options; the slot width eases between word widths so the centred line reflows smoothly.
move: "Built for ___" rolls its gradient word through four options; the slot width eases between word widths so the centred line reflows smoothly.
how: Words are stacked absolutely in a slot clipped vertically by clip-path (sides left open so overhangs never crop). After the font loads each word is measured; every swap moves the outgoing word yPercent 0→-100 and the incoming 100→0 and tweens the slot width, all with cubic-bezier(0.76,0,0.24,1) over 0.75s. Opacity crossfades inside the swap.
adapt: Edit the .word spans; any count works (swaps every 1.25s). Keep the gradient or replace with a solid accent. Placeholder copy is generic; replace it with the product's words. Colours come from the palette tokens at the top of the page (--bg, --surface, --ink, --muted, --accent, --accent-2); change those to re-brand it.
port: All motion is inline in index.html. GSAP pages: register the CustomEase curves, scope selectors to the shot element and rebuild the same timeline; the split helper is inline and dependency-free.
caveats: Original implementation of the After Effects "Rolling text swap" idea; no AE preset files, expressions or numbers are copied and fidelity to a specific AE render is not claimed.
Starts and ends on an empty stage so it loops cleanly; trim the exit when the next shot cuts in.
